name: TUBERCULIN TEST (TT) (Montoux Test)
description: Tuberculin Test (PPD) detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection by measuring delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction. This test screens for latent tuberculosis infection and guides preventive therapy.

testdetails.method: Intradermal Injection with Reading at 48-72 Hours

literatureReview: Tuberculin Skin Test (PPD) detects latent Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. 0.1 mL (5 TU) purified protein derivative injected intradermally on forearm. Read at 48-72 hours by measuring induration (not erythema). Positive: ≥5 mm (HIV+), ≥10 mm (high risk), ≥15 mm (low risk). False negatives in immunocompromised, recent infection, or BCG vaccination. False positives with nontuberculous mycobacteria. Used for LTBI screening in high-risk groups, contact tracing, and pre-biologic therapy evaluation. Positive test indicates infection but not active disease. Follow-up with chest X-ray and consideration of LTBI treatment. Interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) are preferred in BCG-vaccinated individuals.
